messages:
customer-lee: Hi, trying to bring up Redwood Private in our VPC. model pulls fail during deploy. logs show TLS handshake errors to model-registry.redwood.ai:443. can you confirm required outbound hosts?

elaine-support: sorry about that, Lee — can you paste the error snippet? also which installer (helm/docker) and environment (AWS us-east-1 VPC)?

customer-lee: helm chart, aws us-east-1, attaching shortened log: 
```
 2024-11-05T14:02:11Z error: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
 dial tcp 52.23.45.201:443: connect: connection refused
 TLS handshake failed: remote error: tls: bad certificate
```

matt-platform: two things to check quickly: 1) corporate TLS proxy/MITM intercept (breaks cert chain) 2) split-horizon/private DNS resolving model-registry to internal IP that isn't reachable.

ravi-eng: can you run from a node in the cluster: `curl -v https://model-registry.redwood.ai/healthz --resolve model-registry.redwood.ai:443:52.23.45.201` and also `openssl s_client -connect model-registry.redwood.ai:443 -servername model-registry.redwood.ai` and paste results?

customer-lee: ran curl, it times out. openssl shows TLS handshake but `verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate`. Our infra team says we don't MITM TLS, but we do run egress firewall that blocks a bunch.

carlos-network: ok, if you're firewalling egress we publish a minimal allowlist. before that, check DNS from the pod: `kubectl exec -it deploy/installer -- nslookup model-registry.redwood.ai` — if you see a private IP, that's split-horizon and you'll need route/NAT for that prefix.

elaine-support: to be explicit, for Private deployments we recommend whitelisting these FQDNs + ports (and allowing SNI passthrough):
```
- model-registry.redwood.ai:443 (model downloads, metadata)
- auth.redwood.ai:443 (token exchange/OAuth)
- telemetry.redwood.ai:443 (usage/health pings)
- packages.redwood.ai / pypi.org / files.pythonhosted.org:443 (pip installs, wheel pulls)
- artifactory-repo.company.com:443 (if you configured an internal mirror)
- crl.digicert.com, ocsp.digicert.com:80/443 (OCSP/CRL for cert validation)
- time.cloudflare.com or NTP hosts (outbound time sync)
- registry-cc.redwood.ai:443 (container image pulls if using our hosted image registry)
```

ravi-eng: also allow ephemeral IP ranges used by our model CDN — if you can't FQDN-allow, we can provide a CIDR list for your region. will send via secure support ticket.

customer-lee: one thing odd: our egress proxy requires TLS inspection certs to be installed on clients; we don't want to install company CA on the installer nodes. is there a fallback?

matt-platform: two options: 1) disable TLS inspection for the FQDNs above (recommended), or 2) install your CA into the cluster truststore (kube nodes and container images). If you choose option 2, you need to add the CA to the OS trust store and restart nodes so `openssl` and `curl` trust chain resolves.

oncall-bot: @ravi-eng paging: Support escalation for private deploy egress — severity P2.

ravi-eng: for quick repro, please run `curl -I -H \"Host: model-registry.redwood.ai\" https://52.23.45.201/healthz` from a cluster pod. If that succeeds but DNS + name fails, it's DNS/SNI. If IP connect fails, it's firewall.

customer-lee: curl -I to the IP returns 200 but `curl -I https://model-registry.redwood.ai/healthz` fails with TLS verify error. so connecting to ip works, name fails -> likely TLS proxy rewriting cert or you have SNI checks in firewall.

carlos-network: that matches MITM/TLS interception. please verify your proxy does not terminate TLS for `model-registry.redwood.ai`. If it does, you need to allow passthrough or add our CA. Also check your firewall for TLS-SNI filtering.

elaine-support: I'll open a private ticket to share a short CIDR list for the CDN and our support certificate fingerprints to help validate if the proxy is altering chains. In the meantime, try whitelisting hostnames above and allowing direct outbound to port 443.

customer-lee: thanks — quick question about pip installs: our policy blocks direct pypi but allows internal artifactory. can we mirror wheels?

matt-platform: yes, you can use an internal mirror. if you mirror, make sure your artifactory resolves certs correctly and that the installer is configured to use your mirror endpoint via Helm values (`--set installer.pip_index_url=https://artifactory-repo.company.com/simple`). allowlist that artifactory FQDN and also allow access to files.pythonhosted.org if you want optional fallbacks.

ravi-eng: summary of next steps for Lee: 1) run nslookup from pod and share output 2) allowlist the FQDNs listed above (model-registry, auth, telemetry, pypi/artifactory, OCSP/CRL) 3) if TLS inspection is enabled, either disable for those FQDNs or add your CA to cluster truststores 4) open private support ticket for CDN CIDRs + cert fingerprints.

customer-lee: doing nslookup now, will follow up in private ticket. really appreciate the clear checklist! :pray:
